text: Thunderclap Gun Battalion
A thousand flames erupt as one, the roar like thunder—man and horse alike are reduced to ash before it.

The immense trading ports of the Eastern Guard provinces have long channeled vast quantities of firearms both imported and exported, an influence deeply felt in the tactical style of the garrisons stationed here. Before Nangau became Cathay's industrial giant, older firearms produced in the workshops of Fuzhou and Beiqi also played their part in battles across Cathay. Even now, the doctrine of overwhelming firepower remains the mainstream thinking among the border troops and navy of the Eastern Guard\\nSoldiers armed with the thunderclap gun are the elite among marksmen. They must not only carry heavy loads of ammunition and fortification materials, but also master the field maintenance of their gun barrels. Though maintaining such an elite firearms unit is costly, their unmatched firepower has always made them highly sought after
Garrison Spearmen
These garrison-affiliated archers are equipped with spears, effective against harassment from enemy light cavalry.

To counter the ever-growing threat along the Great Bastion, the Northern Guard provinces established garrison towns of all sizes near the wall as an extension of its defenses. Soldiers stationed here often face combat threats far beyond those of ordinary conscripted farmers. As such, only garrison households who have undergone further selection may serve as the defenders here. They are subjected to stricter training and issued higher-quality armor and weapons\\nSpearmen archers are chosen from among the garrison households' most skilled marksmen, and in their hands the heavy longbow unleashes its full power. At the same time, these archers have not neglected their spear training, meaning they do not rely heavily on the cover of allied melee troops
Garrison Crossbowmen
Compared to conscript units, these soldiers have undergone far more rigorous training to bear the weight of guarding the northern frontier.

Skilled with both the broadsword and the sturdy crossbow, they can serve as the mainstay of the defensive line in most situations
Bastion Ironguard (Hammer)
These elite soldiers, chosen from among the hundred, are the cornerstone of the Great Bastion, embodying the northern garrisons' doctrine of offense and defense alike with hammer and crossbow.

Bastion Ironguard are selected from the Jade-Valor border troops who have long served at the frontier of the Great Bastion. They are granted generous provisions and a richer array of weaponry. Under the tactical doctrine of [Lord of Raging Gale] Miao Ying, they have become an elite force combining melee and ranged capability, forming part of the mighty Great Bastion itself\\nAs the numbers of heavily armored Chaos Warriors assaulting the wall have grown, these Ironguard have exchanged their blades for heavy iron maces in response. Their crossbows, though slow to load, compensate with formidable killing power
Bastion Ironguard (Mo Dao)
Wielding Mo Dao blades and powerful crossbows, they charge into the fray—those who meet their edge are shattered, man and steed alike.

Now, rather than volley fire in formation, they yearn to swing their long blades and break the enemy's ranks

They can draw their bows to repel the enemy from great distances, striking the eyes of enemy warhorses or even monsters with precision\\n
Bastion Ironguard (Halberd)
Even with bows slung across their backs, they can still whirl their long halberds with fearsome force.

Even when engaged up close, their hook-bladed halberds can easily drive off enemy cavalry harassment
Gate Overseers
The Gate Overseers guard the pass gates of the Great Bastion's mighty strongholds. Clad in strong armor and skilled with the bow, they are the last safeguard of the ten-thousand-li wall.

Every gate of the Great Bastion's mighty passes is guarded closely by these elite warriors, granted the title of "Gate Overseer." To become a Gate Overseer Cataphract means to receive the recognition of [Lord of Raging Gale] Miao Ying, permitting them to wear the most resplendent armor, wield exquisitely decorated composite bows, and receive a bespoke three-pronged double-edged blade forged specifically for each warrior. This long-hafted great blade is a versatile weapon in combat, capable of countering any foe in these warriors' hands\\nIt is said that [Sentinel] Suitang blesses their finely-crafted bows, allowing each volley of multiple arrows to strike true upon their targets
Garrison Outriders
Silver spears, swift steeds—like wind and lightning—the guardians of the nation face death without fear.

The warhorses ridden by these garrison household riders are notably superior to those found elsewhere in Cathay. Naturally, their duties have never strayed far from danger
Bastion Skyriders
These skyriders defend the skies over Cathay's northern reaches; their fine mobility lets them clear the walls and plunge swiftly into battle.

Under the tactical doctrine of [Lord of Raging Gale] Miao Ying, they have become an elite force combining melee and ranged capability, forming part of the mighty Great Bastion itself\\nCompared to the noble Dragon Horse breed, these winged pegasi carry a far weaker draconic bloodline, with somewhat lesser stamina and burst power. Some claim they are even more closely related to the pegasi of Bretonnia. Even so, they remain an indispensable part of the Great Bastion's defense system. Amid the beacon smoke swirling atop the wall, beneath the blood-red skies of the northern wastes, the Ironguard mounted on these armored winged steeds defend every inch of Cathay's airspace\\n
Thunderscale Cavaliers
Storm dragon-horses wreathed in lightning; their advancing hoofbeats roll like thunder, striking terror into all who hear them.

The Great Bastion, also known as the Dragon's Spine, is the impenetrable colossal defensive work of Cathay's northern frontier. This great wall, personally overseen in its construction by the Dragon Emperor, spans one province after another along the border, and for countless centuries has remained Cathay's first line of defense against Chaos incursions from the north. Such a wonder was built through a defensive system composed of innumerable bricks and stones, and tens of thousands of garrison soldiers unafraid of death. Though Jade-Valor troops from various regions rotate through duty atop the Great Bastion, only the Dragon Spine Guardians remain permanently stationed on this bitter, frozen frontier year-round. As the core strength of the Great Bastion's garrison, they are equipped with heavy blunt weapons, experts at breaking through enemy assaults\\nThe Storm Dragon Horses that live on the eastern grasslands are distant relatives of the Dragon Horse, moving swiftly and known as the "Thunder Qilin." Facing the wasteland's extreme thunderstorms year-round, their scales and single horn seem to hold the power of lightning itself. The Dragon Spine Guardians who ride these noble creatures mount two special war drums upon their steeds; amid their thunderous charges, the surging electric current strikes these drumheads, sounding a soul-stirring war song\\n
Dragongate Chi Riders
These divine beasts bearing great drums are the guardian spirits of the Bastion's Three Passes, appearing only in moments of dire crisis.

Every gate of the Great Bastion's mighty passes is guarded closely by these elite warriors. To stand faithfully at duty before the magnificent gates means to have earned the recognition of [Lord of Raging Gale] Miao Ying, granting them the right to wear the most resplendent armor and wield an exquisitely decorated long spear forged specifically for each warrior. This bladed polearm is a versatile weapon in combat, able to counter any foe in these warriors' hands\\nThe Great Bastion stretches for ten thousand li, crowned with countless mighty passes, among which the Dragon Gate, Serpent Gate, and Turtle Gate stand as the most magnificent. Legend holds that when the Great Bastion was first established, the Sky Dragon Emperor condensed the Winds of Magic into a dragon-headed spirit beast, standing mighty atop the gate towers to guard the three passes. Though the truth of history has long since crumbled into dust alongside countless broken bricks, these legends persist among the soldiers guarding the northern frontier: when thunderous war drums resound across the heavens, a deadlocked battle can turn like lightning, and victory will sprout from the long-parched wasteland like new shoots after a storm\\n
Levy Swordsmen
Answering the call of military merit, these farmers don armor and take up arms—tending the fields within, standing ready for war without.

The conscripted farmers of the Western Guard provinces are called Levies. During their service, if they achieve distinguished military merit, they may exchange the heads they have taken for corresponding land and rank. The more enemies slain, the greater the rise in social status this brings. Though the other Dragon Sons have voiced considerable displeasure at this seemingly backward system, [Lord of Shangyang] Zhao Ming, absorbed in her study of alchemy, appears never to have paid it much mind\\nDrawn by the lure of glory and riches, even the gentlest farmer will take up their ancestral sword and dagger-axe, transforming into a merciless swordsman unafraid of death, hungrily lunging for the enemy's head
Levy Repeater Crossbowmen
The repeating crossbows in their hands loose bolts in rapid succession, more than enough to drive off skaven and goblins that would ravage the fields.

It can unleash a dense hail of arrows over a short distance, requiring little careful aim. Against lightly armored Skaven or Greenskin bandits, these crossbow bolts achieve their maximum effect
Frontier Guards (Ge Halberd)
The armor worn by these polearm-bearing garrison troops is a product of the Western Wards' alchemy, offering protection while channeling the flow of the Winds of Magic.

Though alchemical secrets are strictly forbidden across most of Cathay, this so-called "cunning trickery" found fertile ground to take root in the Western Guard provinces. With the strong backing of [Lord of Shangyang] Zhao Ming, alchemy has been widely applied to the Western Guard's military and production. Though the secret art of permanently affixing magic shields to armor ultimately failed, the byproduct—a material with greatly enhanced magical resistance—was valued and eventually became the primary material for the special armor worn by Western Guard soldiers, capable of repelling and accelerating the flow of the Winds of Magic\\nThese garrison soldiers, promoted from the ranks of Levies, form the main strength of the Western Guard provinces' armies. From driving off wild Orc bandits in the Warpstone Desert to guarding the trade routes of the Fang Road, the presence of these dagger-axe-wielding, heavily armored warriors is felt everywhere
Frontier Guards (Zhanma Sword)
These battle-hardened garrison troops are strong of body, wielding zhanma swords, tasked in the army with breaking the enemy line.

Frontier Guards (Fire Repeater)
A larger crossbow bolt case brings an even more merciless torrent of fire.

Though ordinary repeater crossbows can unleash countless bolts in a short time, the front line's demand for firepower has driven craftsmen to make exaggerated modifications—wider bolt magazines, sturdier slide rails, shorter range, and unmatched burst power\\n
Frontier Guards (Heavy Repeater)
A sky-blackening deluge of arrows will answer every question.

Long Pike Tigerguard
Cathay's western passes have no Great Bastion to shield them, for these warriors are themselves the Wailing Wall of the western provinces.

The elites stationed at Shangyang are all orphans of war, secretly adopted after losing their families, meticulously trained until they don armor and take up arms, forming into companies. After the attempt to mass-produce enchanted armor by incorporating refined warpstone into the forging process failed, [Lord of Shangyang] Zhao Ming personally—or perhaps personally ordered her craftsmen to—forge armor for these personal guards. Though this gesture of kindness weighs heavy, it grants them exceptional protection\\nThese personal guards who fight on foot with long pi-blades are called Tiger Guards. Filled with fervent gratitude for the Dragon Son who raised them, they seem to know no fear, growing ever fiercer when facing massive foes, never yielding a single step\\n
Iron Pagoda Infantry
Before being granted their own guardian stone lion, these warriors must first endure heat within their enchanted armor rivaling that of an alchemical furnace.

When facing fully armed Chaos Warriors and impervious Ogre hordes, these Iron Pagoda troops are the backbone of Cathay's border armies. Clad in armor woven from precisely fitted iron plates, they charge into battle like moving towering pagodas, intercepting the enemy. The heavy blunt weapons wielded by these foot-fighting pagoda warriors are called Demon-Quelling Maces by the people of Cathay; it is said the flames erupting from both ends are fueled by the warrior's own will, extinguishing only alongside their soul when they fall in battle\\nBefore becoming a Gilded Pagoda Rider, every warrior must first fight several battles on foot clad in the heavy pagoda armor, or defeat several Ogre Maneaters bare-handed in single combat at the martial tournaments hosted by [Lord of Shangyang] Zhao Ming, proving superhuman stamina and endurance before being granted their guardian stone lion
Levy Crossbow Riders
While reloading their crossbow bolts, these riders can rely on their steeds' sheer mass to scatter the enemy's light troops.

Conscripted peasants of the Western Provinces are called Levy Soldiers. During their service, if they achieve great military merit, they may exchange the heads of slain enemies for land grants and titles. The more enemies they slay, the higher their social standing rises. Though the other Dragon Sons have voiced considerable displeasure at this seemingly upside-down system, [Lord of Shang Yang] Zhao Ming, ever absorbed in his study of alchemy, has never seemed to give it much thought.\\nThe warhorses of the Western Provinces excel at long treks across the desert rather than high-speed sprints. These mounted archers make full use of this trait, outfitting their horses with full sets of barding, sacrificing a small amount of mobility for greater charging power.
Frontier Cataphracts
Golden spears and iron steeds, a spirit that swallows ten thousand li.

Though alchemical secrets are strictly forbidden across most of Cathay, this [Frivolous Craft] found fertile ground to take root in the Western Provinces. With the strong backing of [Lord of Shang Yang] Zhao Ming, alchemy has been widely applied to Western military affairs and production. Although the secret art of permanently affixing spirit shields to armor ultimately failed, the byproduct—a significant increase in the material's resistance to magic—was recognized as valuable, and eventually became the primary material for the special armor worn by Western frontier guards, which repels and accelerates the flow of the Winds of Magic.\\nThe Western Provinces were among the first regions in Cathay to field armored cavalry. Compared to the more common Jade Valor Lancers, these Frontier Cataphracts hold a significant advantage in both charging infantry and countering enemy cavalry charges.
Inkscale Ironriders
Swift as a soaring feather, steady as an iron forest.

These elites stationed at Shang Yang are all orphans of the battlefield. Secretly adopted after losing their families, they underwent rigorous training until they donned armor and formed into a fighting force. After the attempt to mass-produce enchanted armor by adding refined warpstone to the armor-forging process failed, [Lord of Shang Yang] Zhao Ming personally—or perhaps personally ordered his craftsmen to—forge armor for these bodyguards. This weighty act of kindness nonetheless granted them exceptional protection.\\nThese armored cataphracts, who fight mounted with heavy crossbows, are known as the Plumed Forest Guard. The Boulder Dragon Horses they ride come from the Warpstone Desert, distant relatives of the Grand Dragon Horses. Steadfast and enduring, they are also called the [Ink Qi Lin]. Boulder Dragon Horses lack the explosive power of other subspecies, but generations of long journeys in search of water and grass have honed in them an unparalleled endurance, allowing them to bear heavier riders and vast quantities of arrows, becoming unyielding mobile fortresses of death on the battlefield.\\n
Gilded Pagoda Riders
These mighty warriors, mounted on guardian stone lions, clad in heavy armor and wielding long maces, stand like pagodas, shielding Cathay from every manner of malevolent spirit.

Facing fully-armed Chaos Warriors and armies of unstoppable Ogres, these Iron Pagodas are the backbone of Cathay's frontier armies. Clad in armor woven from precisely fitted iron plates, they ride into battle atop stone guardian lions forged from iron and stone, cutting through the enemy like moving pagoda towers. The blunt weapon wielded by the Iron Pagoda is called the jian by the Cathayans—heavy and forceful, a single swing can easily shatter armor and flesh, inflicting irreparable internal injuries upon the enemy. The stone guardian lion mounts of the Iron Pagoda are the bane of Chaos daemons. As household guardian beasts known throughout Cathay, they were forged with anti-daemonic talismans sealed within by the Dragon Monks of the Celestial Court, capable of weakening and dispelling all manner of fiends and specters.
Garrison Wolfbrush Spearmen
Though the wolfbrush spear is heavy and unwieldy, even raw recruits can grip it and stand firm to meet the enemy.

Dark Elf pirates and Nippon marauders from beyond the Azure Sea have plagued the ports and coastlines of the Eastern Provinces for generations. Against the agile and vicious Ronin and Elf pirates, ordinary peasant levies struggle to hold the line and mount effective counterattacks. Upon returning from a long voyage, [Dragon Fleet Admiral] Yin-Yin ordered his officers to widely recruit farmers and fishermen, training the new recruits in coordinated formation tactics. This quickly formed a fighting force capable of resisting the raiders, reclaiming numerous occupied villages.\\nThese sturdy young men, lacking combat experience but strong of body, are trained to wield the wolf's tooth spear. This cumbersome pike is made from bamboo, with the branches and leaves at its tip left intact and blades bound to it. When formed in ranks, the dense branches can both obstruct the raiders' charge and bolster their allies' morale, stabilizing the line and effectively covering friendly fire.
Garrison Firecracker Gunners
It is said that the din of these firecrackers exploding is enough to frighten off even wicked demons...

Coastal Patrol Guard (Triple-Barrel Gun)

Even having lost out to Nangau's firearms in competition, the garrison troops of the eastern provinces still retain many of these older weapons, hoping to unleash a torrent of firepower before the enemy closes.

Before Nangau became Cathay's industrial titan, older firearms from the workshops of Fu Zhou and Bei Qi also played their part in battles across Cathay. Even now, tactics centered on covering fire remain the mainstream thinking among the Eastern frontier armies and navy.\\nThe triple-barrel gun is a hybrid weapon combining firearm and polearm. Though its short barrels make precise line-of-sight aiming impossible, it retains considerable power and adequate accuracy within thirty or forty paces. After firing, the scorching barrel becomes a heavy blunt weapon for close combat. After the new Iron Hail Gun was widely adopted by Cathay's firearms units, the triple-barrel gun became the exclusive firearm of Eastern Provincial troops. It has also been widely adopted by Coastal Patrol Guards, owing to its suitability for boarding actions in naval warfare.
Coastal Patrol Guard (Halberd-Gun)
These halberds fitted with specialized matchlock guns can fire heavy shot, meant for the sea monsters of the Azure Deep that try to climb aboard the deck.

As such, battalion soldiers equipped with the halberd-gun are often tasked with the critical duty of countering the enemy's large units on the battlefield.
Coastal Patrol Guard (Divine Engine Arrows)
A swarm of burning arrows bursts forth like a horde of bees, earning this gunpowder weapon the name 'the Beehive.'

It has proven true that even when the shots miss their mark, a sky filled with screaming arrows can shatter an enemy's will to resist outright.
Coastal Patrol Guard (Tiger Crouch Cannon)
These heavy gun-barrels shine in siege warfare and street fighting—provided you can find a strong enough man to hoist them up.

Amid the rolling hills of the east, this crude but effective form of rapid artillery support is enough to repel scattered pirates and marauders.\\n
Fire Bomb Throwers
The bravest and most fearless of the garrison troops take up the role of grenadier, hurling the crackling thunder-bombs into the enemy ranks just before they explode.

Even now, tactics centered on covering fire remain the mainstream thinking among the Eastern frontier armies and navy.\\nThese small canister explosives, known as thunderclap bombs, were first used in naval warfare, thrown by sailors onto enemy ships to slaughter their crews. After increasing their powder charge, these weapons became formidable killers against infantry.
Armored Vanguard
The elite warriors of the Vanguard Camp carry iron chains, wear three layers of armor, and advance behind their shields—impervious to blade and spear alike.

Long before Cathay's unification, nomadic tribes from the north posed a grave threat to the central plains' regimes, their armored warriors the stuff of nightmares for Han soldiers. These elite infantry call themselves Bayara, meaning "vanguard warriors." Covered from head to toe in cloth-faced iron armor, they gain superior ranged defense compared to lamellar armor while greatly reducing weight. This makes them well suited to long-range raids, concentrating superior force to break through enemy formations. Now, at the Dragon Emperor's call, former mortal enemies will stand shoulder to shoulder against the forces of destruction beyond the Azure Sea, together guarding Cathay's eternal peace.\\nBefore scaling a wall, these vanguard warriors throw iron darts to weaken the defenders atop the ramparts. In battle, they excel at using heavy shield bashes to force the enemy off the wall's edge, swiftly seizing control of the ramparts.
Dragonship Marines
The decks of the Dragon Ships of the Deep are guarded by these sentinels bearing mysterious firearms, the linchpin of firepower on the battlefield.

Though light cloth-faced armor is better suited to fighting aboard ship, these elite guardians stationed on the warships of the Azure Sea still wear closely-fitted scale armor, engraved with ornate patterns—likely a reflection of their additional ceremonial duties. To [Dragon Fleet Admiral] Yin-Yin, the fleet's magnificent bearing matters just as much as victory in battle; on this point, there is no room for doubt.\\nAs the elite guard protecting the deck, Dragonship Marines rarely take part in boarding actions or amphibious landings. Their duty is usually to pour a hail of ammunition across the enemy formation from the ship's deck, dominating the entire battlefield. Of course, this does not mean they lack skill in close combat—amid the countless unspeakable horrors lurking beneath the Azure Sea, the long halberds in the hands of the Dragonship Marines become the ship's final line of defense.\\n
Garrison Fire Lancers
The grief and hatred of a broken nation and shattered families fuel them as they charge into the enemy ranks, wielding fiercely burning lances.

Those left desperate and ruined by pirate raids willingly take up these dangerous weapons, mount fire-fearless steeds, and hurl themselves into the enemy's ranks, hunting down the foes they can never forgive.\\n
Wavebreaker Dragon Riders
This noble-looking creature of the deep seas is rumored to be a distant kin of the dragons; it chooses its own rider, one it deems worthy, to campaign together across the azure waves.

Though light cloth-faced armor is better suited to fighting aboard ship, these elite guardians stationed on the warships of the Azure Sea still wear closely-fitted scale armor, engraved with ornate patterns—likely a reflection of their additional ceremonial duties. To [Dragon Fleet Admiral] Yin-Yin, the fleet's magnificent bearing matters just as much as victory in battle; on this point, there is no room for doubt.\\nThe Jiao Long, said to be a surviving bloodline of Cathay's ancient dragon race, remain mysterious and unfathomable, lurking for years beneath the surging waves of the Azure Sea. Only the thunderous roar of a treasure ship cleaving through the waves can summon them forth to join the grand fleet's distant patrols. A select few rigorously trained marines can fight alongside these massive sea beasts, mercilessly devouring the enemy in smoke and towering waves.\\n
Hunter Spearmen
These hunters have roamed the Mountains of Heaven for generations; their keen instincts and deep experience can be trusted absolutely.

The Southern Provinces are dominated by hills and mountains, and its people largely make their living through hunting. These hunters have spent years locked in combat with vicious Beastmen, cold-blooded Snakemen, and ever-changing Simian folk, accumulating invaluable experience in navigating the jungle. Garrison troops stationed in the Southern Provinces often hire them as scouts or guides, and these hunters are equally happy to gather rich spoils after major battles.\\nHunter Spearmen, raised from childhood in the southern lands, wield hunting spears that may not be sharp, but strike true with every blow. With hounds at their side, they remain a force to be reckoned with even on the battlefield.
Hunter Slingers
These venomous pellets are made from a blend of poisonous herbs gathered by hunters and venom drawn from Snake-Men, potent enough to fell even the fiercest beasts of the jungle.

Blademaster Champions
Ogres of raw physical might are common enough, but only those blessed with both wisdom and courage may bear great responsibility.

After a falling comet destroyed the homeland of the Ogres, some Ogre tribes living along Cathay's borders chose to remain, embracing assimilation into Cathayan civilization. With their towering builds and boundless strength, they earned the Cathayan honorific title of "Swordmaster," and gradually became an indispensable part of Cathay's military system.
